entities.name: Ariobarzanes II of Cappadocia
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ariobarzanes II of Cappadocia (b. 89 BCE) was a key figure in the Hellenistic era, playing a pivotal role in the complex politics of the region.

As the ruler of Cappadocia, Ariobarzanes II maintained a delicate balance between his kingdom and the expanding Roman Empire, navigating a treacherous landscape of alliances and rivalries.

His economic policies, which emphasized trade and commerce, contributed to the growth of Cappadocia's wealth and influence, making him a notable figure in the economic history of the region.

Ariobarzanes II's legacy can be seen in the continued presence of Hellenistic culture in Cappadocia, as well as the Roman Empire's eventual absorption of the kingdom.

'In the pursuit of peace and prosperity, we must be willing to make difficult choices and adapt to the changing tides of history.' - Ariobarzanes II of Cappadocia
